main_text.p: Senatus Areopagiticus ius dicito de cæde, aut vulnere, non casu, sed voluntate, inflicto, de incendio item, malo veneno hominis necandi causa dato.
Neq; orâtes præfantor, neq; affectus mouento, neq; extra rem dicunto.
Siquis hominem sciens morti duit, capital esto.
Thesmothetæ in homicidas animadvertunto.
Homicidas morte multanto in patria occisi terra, & abducunto, vt Lege cautum est; in eos ne sæuiunto, neue pecuniam exigunto.

page.notes: Greek passages and the Atticist law text are transcribed from a small, blurred scan; many Greek words are doubtful and marked [?] or illegible. The numbered laws at the start of lines are printed section numbers and are kept in the paragraphs. Left edge of the column is cut off, so the first words of several lines are missing; the top fragment above the first paragraph is unreadable. The italic line "ij qui in proelijs..." begins at the cut and may be the end of a longer heading or rubric. The word before "SEPTIMVS" and before "PRIMVS" (LIBER / CAPUT or similar) is cut off; the "S" before PRIMVS is partly visible. The heading "Sicarijs." is partly cut at the left, so its first letter is uncertain. No page number or running head is visible.
